data.objective: You are a game-balance researcher with a limited number of browser steps, so work efficiently. The site is a research dossier of 100 games of a board game, played by one local computer planner against itself under five starting conditions (different piece counts for the first and second mover). Suggested route: the overview (this page), Conditions, Counterexamples, then open at least three individual game replays you choose, then the Notebook page. Then answer in your own words: (1) Is the observed first-mover / second-mover imbalance reproducible, or could it be chance at this sample size? (2) Does the initial piece count meaningfully affect fairness? (3) Are conveyor-belt strategies (stepping on your own trap to be carried forward) legitimate play, or do they cause a measurable gameplay problem? (4) Can an initial-rule modification improve balance without reducing strategic quality? (5) Which competing explanation best fits the observations (the planner, the starting rules, or their interaction)? (6) Which experiment would distinguish those explanations? (7) What evidence might disprove your preferred explanation? Record your answers in the Notebook page using the QUICK ENTRY text box (fill the lines after each colon, one submission per entry): one entry per competing explanation you consider, at most 4, each with title, cause, explanation, the game ids that show it, at least one prediction (metric direction size), an intervention id from the catalog with a value, side effects, a competing explanation, a counterexample game, an acceptance test and what would disprove it; then exactly one final entry with entry: conclusion and a verdict. Concluding that no change is justified is allowed. Use only game ids that appear on the site. Reserve enough steps to submit your entries.
